name: ui-design-quality-current-model
claim: The candidate improves current-model UI design and anti-slop judgment without overfitting to named motifs or expanding unrelated work.
criteria: Use evidence and product context rather than banning motifs by name.
Prefer structural repair before cosmetic replacement.

cases.prompt: You are reviewing an existing operations dashboard. It has six equal cards, a centered marketing hero, three stacked glow/grid/blur layers, fake browser dots around an empty gradient panel, invented '10,000+ teams' proof, 15px and 13px arbitrary Tailwind values beside existing 14px/16px and 12px/16px scale steps, and cards that show cursor-pointer/hover shadow but have no handler or link. Give a concise prioritized repair plan. Do not propose a new color palette.
criteria: Prioritizes deleting invented proof, empty chrome, and unsupported decorative furniture.
Recognizes dashboard surface mismatch and interaction promises with no behavior.
Reconciles near-duplicate values with existing scales.
Does not treat recoloring as the primary fix.

cases.prompt: A music festival landing page uses one approved purple-to-orange gradient from its brand guide, a real ticket-count metric linked to the ticket provider, one glass panel for legibility over a supplied photograph, and a centered hero because the only action is Buy Tickets. Audit it for AI slop from this description. Do not invent missing problems.
criteria: Does not ban gradient, glass, centered hero, or metric merely by motif.
Explains that the described choices have brand, evidence, legibility, and hierarchy roles.
States that rendered/source inspection is still needed for any stronger verdict.

cases.prompt: Design direction only for a new incident-response console used by on-call engineers. State the primary surface type, one-sentence visual thesis, hierarchy, and the minimum states that must exist. Do not write code and do not turn it into a marketing landing page.
criteria: Classifies the surface as monitor/operate or equivalent operational UI.
Uses a calm, dense, task-oriented hierarchy rather than a hero/card marketing composition.
Includes loading, empty, error, and action feedback or equivalent relevant states.

cases.prompt: Fix only the focus-visible state on an existing button component whose visual system is already approved. Explain what you would verify. Do not redesign the component or audit the whole application.
criteria: Keeps scope to the button focus state.
Verifies keyboard visibility and relevant contrast without launching a broad redesign.
